primitives.name: Ridge Regularization
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Ridge** — shrinks all coefficients; offensive players load on direct, defensive on indirect.
primitives.assumptions: All coefficients are shrunk equally; assumes linear relationship between features and outcome.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When feature multicollinearity is high, leading to unstable estimates.

layer2.mapping: Ridge regularization acts as a kernel smoother in player rating space, reducing variance at cost of bias.
layer2.telemetry: Mean squared error of player ratings against ground truth match outcomes.

primitives.name: Group Lasso
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Group lasso** — 8 groups (4 positions × direct/indirect); group-level selection, ridge-like within group.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'β_g': 'coefficient vector for group g (dimensionless)', 'w_g': 'weight for group g (dimensionless)', 'λ': 'regularization parameter (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Player roles are grouped by position and involvement type; group-wise sparsity is desired.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When inter-group correlations are strong but intra-group independence holds.

layer2.mapping: Group lasso enables position-aware player evaluation by enforcing joint selection across role types.
layer2.telemetry: Number of selected players per position group in match outcome prediction models.

primitives.name: Exclusive Lasso
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Exclusive lasso** — ridge between groups, lasso within: selects a few standouts per group (scouting use case).
primitives.assumptions: Only one standout player per role group contributes significantly; encourages sparse selection.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When group-level diversity is low or when individual player impact is not well-separated.

layer2.mapping: Exclusive lasso acts as a rank-order selector for top contributors within each role category.
layer2.telemetry: Top-k player rankings per role group used in scouting reports.

primitives.name: Generalized Lasso
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Generalized (ranking) lasso** — fused/ranking penalty clustering similar-strength players into equivalence classes, separately for direct and indirect coefficients.
primitives.assumptions: Players with similar strengths are grouped; ranking penalties enforce smoothness in coefficient ordering.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When player strength differences are minimal or when ranking is inconsistent with observed outcomes.

layer2.mapping: Generalized lasso clusters players into equivalence classes based on contribution similarity, aiding in team composition modeling.
layer2.telemetry: Equivalence class sizes and stability under cross-validation for match outcome predictions.

The core insight of this work lies in decomposing football possession sequences into direct and indirect player contributions through structured regularization. The ridge penalty ensures stable estimation by shrinking all coefficients, while the group lasso enforces role-based grouping to distinguish offensive from defensive impacts. The exclusive lasso introduces a hard threshold per group, useful for identifying standout performers. The generalized lasso adds a ranking constraint that clusters players with similar impact levels, improving interpretability. These primitives form a hierarchy of increasing sophistication in capturing player behavior. The mathematical duality between these penalties and their empirical performance reveals that structured shrinkage improves predictive validity over classical methods like ELO or xG. Failure modes include overfitting due to insufficient data, misalignment of position groups, and incorrect assumptions about causality in possession features. The conic programming formulation allows scalable optimization, making it suitable for large-scale sports analytics pipelines.
